growth_thesis.claim: Demand-led RevPAR growth is the main driver: Comparable Hotels RevPAR rose 7.3% in the third quarter to $133.60 from $124.55, with ADR up 4.3% and occupancy up 2.8%.
quotes: Momentum continued to build during the third quarter, with broad-based demand from both business and leisure travelers driving Comparable Hotels RevPAR growth of more than 7% as compared to the same period last year.

growth_thesis.basis: Margin and expense figures are stated in the release; the cost-pressure counter is stated in the 10-K and 10-Q; the mechanism is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Operating leverage on that revenue is a second driver: Comparable Hotels Adjusted Hotel EBITDA margin was 37.1% against 35.0%, because Comparable Hotels revenue grew 8.2% while Comparable Hotels operating expenses grew 4.7%.
quotes: Our asset management and property teams leveraged our efficient operating model to convert top-line gains into approximately 210 basis points of Comparable Hotels Adjusted Hotel EBITDA Margin expansion and an increase in Adjusted EBITDAre of more than 13%.
The Company continues to feel upward pressure on total payroll costs given a competitive labor market where the demand for strong hotel talent remains high.

growth_thesis.claim: Management raised its 2026 outlook on this momentum, guiding net income of $177 Million to $192 Million, Comparable Hotels RevPAR change of 5.1% to 6.1%, and Adjusted EBITDAre of $482 Million to $493 Million. The guide holds only if fourth-quarter demand stays strong.
quotes: The revised guidance range reflects the Company’s stronger-than-anticipated third quarter 2026 performance and an increase in its outlook for the fourth quarter, driven by continued improvement in business and leisure travel demand.

growth_thesis.basis: Intent and contracts are stated; the effect on growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Capital recycling is a stated growth lever, but it is not yet visible in results. Five hotels are under contract for sale for a combined $71.8 million, and management intends to redeploy proceeds into acquisitions. No hotels were acquired in the first nine months, and the owned count fell to 216 from 220.
quotes: Supported by a strong balance sheet and significant available liquidity, we are actively underwriting acquisition opportunities, and we intend to redeploy proceeds into hotels that further enhance the quality and growth profile of our portfolio.
During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company did not acquire any properties and sold one property on April 15, 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-Q and release; the slip is read from the two filings.
growth_thesis.claim: Contracted future supply is a longer-dated driver: a $65.5 million forward purchase of a 160-room AC Hotel in Anchorage and a dual-branded Las Vegas development of about $143.7 million, of which $16.9 million had been capitalized. The 10-Q puts the Las Vegas opening in the third quarter of 2028, later than the second quarter in the 10-K.
quotes: There are many conditions to closing on this hotel that have not yet been satisfied, and there can be no assurance that closing on this hotel will occur under the outstanding purchase contract.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release; the balance sheet shows debt, net of 1,479,113 (table in thousands); the link to growth capacity is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Balance-sheet capacity is the condition that lets the company fund acquisitions, development and renovations. Net debt to total capitalization was 27.5%, there were no revolver borrowings, about $700 million of revolver availability, and no significant maturities until 2029.
quotes: Following the completion of these refinancing transactions, the Company has no significant debt maturities until 2029, reinforcing Apple Hospitality’s conservative, well-laddered debt maturity schedule and financial flexibility.

growth_thesis.basis: Spending plan stated in the release; the growth benefit is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Continued reinvestment in the existing hotels supports competitiveness. Management guides 2026 capital expenditures of $85 Million to $95 Million, including renovations at about 18 hotels, and says they are prioritized toward the highest-return opportunities.
quotes: Apple Hospitality consistently reinvests in its hotels to maintain and enhance each property’s relevance and competitive position within its respective market.

growth_thesis.basis: Management view stated in the release; risks stated in the 10-K; the condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: For growth to continue into 2027, demand must stay firm and new hotel supply must stay muted, as management asserts. Lodging is described as highly cyclical and tied to the general economy.
quotes: As we look ahead to 2027, sustained demand momentum and muted new supply create a meaningful tailwind for our portfolio, and we expect to build on this year’s results to deliver continued growth and attractive returns for our shareholders.
The performance of the lodging industry has historically been highly cyclical and closely linked to the performance of the general economy both nationally and within local markets in the U.S.

material_events.claim: The company recognized an impairment loss of about $4.3 million in Q3 2026 on a hotel held for sale, written down to fair value less costs to sell based on the contracted sales price.
quotes: The fourth hotel held for sale was recorded at its estimated fair value less costs to sell, which was based on the contracted sales price, resulting in an impairment loss recognized during the third quarter of 2026.
In connection with these sale contracts, in the third quarter 2026, the Company recognized an impairment loss of approximately $4.3 million with respect to one of the hotels under contract for sale.

material_events.claim: The company amended and restated its unsecured $1.2 billion credit facility, raising capacity to about $1.3 billion, extending maturities and improving pricing. It also increased and extended its term loan.
quotes: In July 2026, the Company amended and restated its existing unsecured $1.2 billion credit facility
increasing the borrowing capacity to approximately $1.3 billion

material_events.claim: The company signed agreements to sell four hotels for an aggregate gross price of $50.3 million. They are classified as held for sale, with closings expected in Q4 2026.
quotes: In addition, during the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company entered into three purchase and sale agreements with two unrelated parties to sell four hotels for an aggregate gross sales price of $50.3 million.

material_events.claim: After quarter-end the company agreed to sell one more hotel for about $21.5 million, with closing expected in Q4 2026.
quotes: Subsequent to the end of the quarter, in October 2026, the Company entered into a purchase and sale agreement with an unrelated party for the sale of one hotel for a gross sales price of approximately $21.5 million.

material_events.claim: After quarter-end the company repaid in full one mortgage loan secured by three properties, about $49.6 million in total.
quotes: Subsequent to the end of the third quarter, the Company repaid in full one mortgage loan secured by three of its properties, for a total of approximately $49.6 million

material_events.claim: In its Q3 earnings release the company updated its 2026 outlook upward. Net income guidance is $177 Million to $192 Million.
quotes: The Company is updating its operational and financial outlook for 2026.

risks.basis: The comparison effect is stated in the cited release and 10-K. The size of the effect is not given, so how much of the growth is rebound is inferred.
risks.claim: Part of the reported demand recovery is measured against a weak prior-year base hurt by the government shutdown, so growth may slow as those comparisons ease. Third-quarter Comparable Hotels RevPAR rose 7.3% and preliminary October growth is about 10%.
quotes: reflecting strength well beyond the easier comparison to last year’s government shutdown
favorable comparisons to prior periods impacted by government-related disruptions

risks.basis: The guidance range and its drivers are stated in the release. The risk of a cut is inferred.
risks.claim: The raised 2026 guidance depends on a stronger fourth quarter. It covers Comparable Hotels RevPAR growth of 5.1% to 6.1% and excludes unannounced acquisitions and dispositions. A fourth-quarter shortfall would force the range to be cut.
quotes: The revised guidance range reflects the Company’s stronger-than-anticipated third quarter 2026 performance and an increase in its outlook for the fourth quarter, driven by continued improvement in business and leisure travel demand.

risks.basis: The conditions and the lack of assurance are stated in the cited items. The risk of impairment or delay is inferred.
risks.claim: Planned disposals may not close or may generate impairments. Five hotels are under contract for a combined $71.8 million, and the company recorded a $4.3 million impairment on one hotel held for sale in the third quarter.
quotes: there can be no assurance that closings on the sales of these hotels will occur under the outstanding sale agreements

risks.basis: The interest-rate exposure is stated in the 10-K risk factors and the liquidity figures in the release. How much debt is currently unhedged in 2026 is not in the evidence, so the exposure's current size is inferred.
risks.claim: Variable-rate debt and refinancing expose the company to higher interest costs. Total debt outstanding is $1,490,262 (table in thousands), mostly on unsecured credit facilities, and swap expirations and replacements affect how much of it is fixed.
quotes: The Company is also subject to risks associated with increases in interest rates with respect to the Company’s variable-rate debt which could reduce cash from operations and adversely affect its ability to make distributions to shareholders.

risks.basis: The cost figures and the fixed-cost language are stated in the cited items. The margin-squeeze scenario is inferred.
risks.claim: Fixed and rising costs can erode margins if demand weakens. Third-quarter general and administrative expense rose 45.0% to 10,915 (table in thousands), and hotel costs are partly fixed.
quotes: These hotel operating expenses generally do not decrease when hotel revenues decrease
